tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

### What happens
`recording.mp4` (0:32) shows a small yard: two floating elements hang side by side, and a penguin
walks a loop in front of them, carrying a smaller floating element above its head. Seen from the
front, all three floating elements are set up to display the same thing. From about 0:15 the camera

Each of these elements displays exactly what it was set up to display, at every moment and from
every side it is seen from. This must hold for any such element anywhere in the world and however it

All.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier. Resets every path test.patch touches to the immutable harbor_base tag, applies
# the hidden tests, runs ONLY the configured f2p + p2p tests with the repository's own runner into a
# JUnit report, and lets verifier.py turn that report into the reward. Nothing here reads the
# candidate's source to decide anything.
set -uo pipefail

# ---- task-specific values, filled by the task builder ----------------------------------------
# run_tests runs the configured tests with the repository's own runner and writes JUnit XML to
# $JUNIT_OUT. The test ids (f2p + p2p from /tests/config.json) are in $TEST_IDS_FILE, one per line.
# Write plain shell commands here; no quoting of the whole block is needed.
run_tests() {
  cmake --build build --parallel 2
  python3 tests/harvest_c01/run_test.py --junit-out "$JUNIT_OUT"
}
# Directories holding the repo's test plumbing (configs, helpers) that must also be restored so a
# candidate cannot replace the harness. Space-separated, relative to /app; '' if none.
PROTECTED_DIRS='games/devtest'
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
export JUNIT_OUT=/logs/verifier/junit.xml
export TEST_IDS_FILE=/logs/verifier/test_ids.txt
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"
rm -f "$JUNIT_OUT" /logs/verifier/reward.txt /logs/verifier/reward.json

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# Capture the agent's submission BEFORE anything below mutates /app -- this is the last
# moment the tree is base + agent work; the restore loop and test.patch come next.
#
# A THROWAWAY INDEX, never /app/.git/index: `git add` against the real one would leave paths
# staged and change how the `git checkout harbor_base --` and `git clean` below behave.
#
# TRACKED EDITS + A SOURCE WHITELIST, not `add -A` with a blacklist. This image builds wx
# in-tree AFTER the harbor_base commit (environment/Dockerfile), so everything the build
# emits is untracked and NOT in wx's .gitignore. A bare `add -A` captured 380MB of .o/.d/.so;
# excluding those by extension still left ~120 configure-generated files (samples/*/Makefile,
# bk-deps, version-script, lib/wx/config/*, the utils/wxrc/wxrc binary) because most have no
# extension to blacklist. Inverting it -- stage tracked modifications, then add only untracked
# files that LOOK like source -- keeps the agent's work and drops generated output by default.
_SUB=/logs/verifier/submission.patch
_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index
_SUBSRC=('*.c' '*.cc' '*.cpp' '*.cxx' '*.h' '*.hh' '*.hpp' '*.hxx' '*.inl' '*.m' '*.mm'
         '*.py' '*.rb' '*.go' '*.rs' '*.java' '*.js' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.cs' '*.kt' '*.swift')
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app read-tree harbor_base 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -u 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
# Enumerate before adding: `git add` aborts and stages NOTHING if any one pathspec matches
# no file, which silently drops the agent's new files on most tasks.
# Generated-output dirs are dropped from the UNTRACKED scan only. A project that keeps real
# source under lib/ is unaffected: those files are tracked at harbor_base, so `add -u` above
# already has them. This drops only files CREATED under a build dir during the run -- which,
# left in, break replay: they are recorded as new-file hunks and a fresh container from the
# same image already has them, so `git apply` fails with "already exists in working directory".
mapfile -t _SUBNEW < <(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard \
  -- "${_SUBSRC[@]}" ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' 2>/dev/null)
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -- "${_SUBNEW[@]}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
fi
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app diff --binary --cached harbor_base \
  > "$_SUB" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"

# WHAT THE WHITELIST DROPPED, listed rather than silently discarded. The split above captures
# every change to a TRACKED file (any extension, deletions included) but only NEW files that
# look like source -- so an agent adding config.yml, a .cmake module or an extensionless script
# loses it, and the patch still looks clean. That is the failure this manifest exists to expose.
#
# NEWEST FIRST, which is the useful ordering and not a cosmetic one: build output and image
# assets are created before the agent phase starts, so anything the agent made sorts to the top.
# Build artifacts are excluded by the same rules as the capture, to keep the list readable.
#
# If something here belongs in the submission, widen _SUBSRC. Do not reach for `add -A`.
_SUBSKIP=/logs/verifier/submission-skipped.txt
_SUBCAP=/tmp/.submission_captured
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then printf '%s\n' "${_SUBNEW[@]}" > "$_SUBCAP"; else : > "$_SUBCAP"; fi
_SUBSKIPN=$(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
    ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
    ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
    ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
{ echo "# Untracked files NOT captured into submission.patch, newest first."
  echo "# Anything the agent created sorts above build output, which predates the agent phase."
  echo "# total: ${_SUBSKIPN}  (showing at most 40)"
  git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
      ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
      ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
      ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | head -200 \
    | while IFS= read -r _f; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(stat -c %Y "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" \
                              "$(stat -c %s "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$_f"
      done \
    | sort -rn | head -40 | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n",$1,$2,$3}'
} > "$_SUBSKIP" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$_SUBCAP"

# Size guard. The whitelist is a heuristic, so a task laying out source unusually could still
# produce something enormous. Cap it and leave a diagnosable stub: a truncated capture is
# recoverable, a full disk is not.
_SUBSZ=$(wc -c < "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "$_SUBSZ" -gt 5242880 ]; then
  { echo "SUBMISSION CAPTURE SUPPRESSED: ${_SUBSZ} bytes exceeds the 5MB cap."
    echo "Directories contributing to the discarded patch:"
    grep -a "^diff --git" "$_SUB" | sed 's#^diff --git a/##; s# b/.*##; s#/[^/]*$##' \
      | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
  } > "$_SUB.suppressed" 2>/dev/null
  : > "$_SUB"
  echo "== submission.patch SUPPRESSED (${_SUBSZ} bytes > 5MB cap) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
else
  echo "== captured submission.patch (${_SUBSZ} bytes, $(grep -ac '^diff --git' "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) files) ==" \
    | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
fi


# 1. Restore every path test.patch touches. Both diff headers are read, so new files, binary
#    baselines (image-comparison PNGs, snapshots), renames and deletions are all covered.
_patch_paths=$( { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
                  sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch; } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done
for _d in $PROTECTED_DIRS; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_d" 2>/dev/null || true
  git -C /app clean -fdq -- "$_d" 2>/dev/null || true
done

# 2. Apply the hidden tests.
echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# 3. Run only the configured tests.
python3 - <<'PY' > "$TEST_IDS_FILE"
import json
c = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
print("\n".join(c["f2p"] + c["p2p"]))
PY
echo "== running f2p + p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
( cd /app && run_tests ) >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(tests exited non-zero; parsing the report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

# 4. Reward from the report.
echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Rubric judge — SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
# nothing; scoring falls back to tests alone. Once a judge sub-agent has written
# verdict.json there, `mm_run.sh <task> rescore` folds the verdict into the reward.
# The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}"
fi

python3 /tests/verifier.py "${REPORTS[@]}" --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}"

echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Behavioral tests for sprite / upright_sprite entities.
+
+Runs the real compiled client+singleplayer-server headlessly under Xvfb with
+software OpenGL (Mesa llvmpipe), using the devtest game plus the sprite_probe
+world mod, which places a fixed set of probe entities around a motionless,
+fixed-look player (see worldmods/sprite_probe/init.lua):
+
+  view A (looking +Z): the devtest animated upright_sprite next to an otherwise
+      identical camera-facing sprite; a camera-facing sprite and two upright
+      sprites (one showing its front, one its back) with a texture made of four
+      differently coloured quadrants; an animated camera-facing sprite and an
+      animated upright sprite, each attached to another object; an upright
+      sprite whose frame the mod changes with set_sprite() once per second.
+  views B (looking -Z) and C (looking +X): four camera-facing sprites using
+      select_x_by_camera with a 6-column sheet (one solid colour per column),
+      turned to yaw 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees.
+
+The client's own rendered framebuffer is captured (ffmpeg x11grab, single
+frame) repeatedly, and the dominant colour of fixed screen regions is
+classified against the probe textures' colours.
+
+Usage:
+    run_test.py --junit-out PATH [TEST_ID ...]
+
+With no TEST_ID arguments, all known tests are run and reported.
+"""
+import argparse
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from PIL import Image
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+MINETEST_BIN = os.environ.get("MINETEST_BIN", "/app/bin/minetest")
+DISPLAY_NUM = os.environ.get("HARVEST_DISPLAY", ":99")
+SCREEN_W, SCREEN_H = 1280, 720
+
+# Screen-space sample boxes (x0, y0, x1, y1), determined empirically for the
+# fixed camera/entity layout in worldmods/sprite_probe/init.lua.
+# View A
+UPRIGHT_BOX = (326, 316, 456, 444)
+REF_BOX = (820, 316, 954, 444)
+UPRIGHT_BACK_BOX = (326, 100, 456, 232)    # upright sprite, back towards the camera
+SPRITE_QUADS_BOX = (820, 100, 954, 232)    # camera-facing sprite
+UPRIGHT_FRONT_BOX = (326, 530, 456, 660)   # upright sprite, front towards the camera
+ATTACHED_BOX = (820, 530, 954, 660)        # animated sprite attached to another object
+ATTACHED_UPRIGHT_BOX = (32, 316, 160, 444)             # animated upright sprite attached to another object
+STEPPED_BOX = (1120, 316, 1248, 444)             # upright sprite stepped by set_sprite() every second
+# Views B and C: one box per probe sprite, yaw 0, 90, 180, 270 degrees
+VIEW_B_BOXES = [(758, 340, 818, 400), (658, 340, 720, 400), (560, 340, 620, 400), (460, 340, 522, 400)]
+VIEW_C_BOXES = VIEW_B_BOXES
+
+SAMPLE_INTERVAL = 0.4
+SAMPLE_WINDOW = 10.0
+VIEW_SAMPLES = 5
+ATTEMPTS = 2           # the scenario is run again if the harness itself fails (client crash, timeout)
+FRAME_LENGTH = 1.0     # seconds per frame of every animated probe
+
+PALETTE = {
+    "yellow": (255, 240, 0),
+    "red": (255, 57, 57),
+    "magenta": (204, 57, 255),
+    "blue": (72, 83, 255),
+}
+# frame order of the animated sheet (testnodes_anim.png, rows top to bottom)
+CYCLE = ["yellow", "red", "magenta", "blue"]
+QUADS = {
+    "top_left": (40, 200, 40),
+    "top_right": (255, 128, 0),
+    "bottom_left": (150, 60, 230),
+    "bottom_right": (0, 200, 220),
+}
+# select_x_by_camera sheet: column -> colour
+COLUMNS = {
+    "front": (255, 57, 57),      # 1st column: subject facing the camera
+    "left": (40, 200, 40),       # 2nd column: subject looking to the left
+    "back": (72, 83, 255),       # 3rd column: subject backing the camera
+    "right": (255, 240, 0),      # 4th column: subject looking to the right
+    "above": (255, 255, 255),    # 5th column: subject viewed from above
+    "below": (20, 20, 20),       # 6th column: subject viewed from below
+}
+# Which side of a subject turned to yaw 0/90/180/270 degrees faces the camera.
+# Entity yaw 0 faces +X, and a positive yaw turns it towards +Z (the same
+# convention automatic_face_movement_dir uses: yaw = atan2(vel.z, vel.x)).
+# View B looks along -Z, view C along +X.
+EXPECTED_B = ["left", "front", "right", "back"]
+EXPECTED_C = ["back", "left", "front", "right"]
+
+ALL_TEST_IDS = [
+    "sprite_probe.upright_sprite_renders_a_palette_color",
+    "sprite_probe.reference_sprite_renders_a_palette_color",
+    "sprite_probe.upright_sprite_animates",
+    "sprite_probe.reference_sprite_animates",
+    "sprite_probe.upright_sprite_follows_set_sprite",
+    "sprite_probe.sprite_texture_is_not_mirrored",
+    "sprite_probe.upright_sprite_back_is_not_mirrored",
+    "sprite_probe.upright_sprite_front_is_not_mirrored",
+    "sprite_probe.attached_sprite_animates",
+    "sprite_probe.attached_upright_sprite_animates",
+    "sprite_probe.camera_facing_sprite_shows_the_side_facing_the_camera",
+]
+
+
+def classify(rgb, palette=PALETTE):
+    best, best_d = None, None
+    for name, ref in palette.items():
+        d = sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(rgb, ref))
+        if best_d is None or d < best_d:
+            best, best_d = name, d
+    return best, best_d
+
+
+def classify_shaded(rgb, palette):
+    """Nearest palette colour, allowing each colour to be dimmed or brightened
+    by a constant factor (entity shading depends on which way a quad faces)."""
+    best, best_d = None, None
+    for name, ref in palette.items():
+        rr = sum(c * c for c in ref) or 1.0
+        s = min(1.15, max(0.35, sum(a * b for a, b in zip(rgb, ref)) / rr))
+        d = sum((a - s * b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(rgb, ref))
+        if best_d is None or d < best_d:
+            best, best_d = name, d
+    return best, best_d
+
+
+def dominant_color(img, box):
+    """Most common color in the box, quantized to tolerate dithering/AA noise.
+
+    The sample box covers a textured quad (solid colour fields, possibly with
+    a thin border or a letter glyph). The background is the single largest
+    contiguous color, so its (quantized) mode is a much more robust signal
+    than the mean -- the mean gets pulled toward black by border and glyph
+    pixels.
+    """
+    crop = img.crop(box).convert("RGB")
+    buckets = {}
+    step = 16
+    for p in crop.getdata():
+        key = (p[0] // step, p[1] // step, p[2] // step)
+        bucket = buckets.setdefault(key, [0, 0, 0, 0])
+        bucket[0] += p[0]
+        bucket[1] += p[1]
+        bucket[2] += p[2]
+        bucket[3] += 1
+    best_key = max(buckets, key=lambda k: buckets[k][3])
+    r, g, b, n = buckets[best_key]
+    return (r / n, g / n, b / n)
+
+
+def corners(box):
+    """The four corner ninths of a box (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right)."""
+    x0, y0, x1, y1 = box
+    w, h = (x1 - x0) // 3, (y1 - y0) // 3
+    return {
+        "top_left": (x0, y0, x0 + w, y0 + h),
+        "top_right": (x1 - w, y0, x1, y0 + h),
+        "bottom_left": (x0, y1 - h, x0 + w, y1),
+        "bottom_right": (x1 - w, y1 - h, x1, y1),
+    }
+
+
+def majority(names):
+    return Counter(names).most_common(1)[0][0] if names else None
+
+
+def wait_for_x(display, timeout=20):
+    deadline = time.time() + timeout
+    sock_path = f"/tmp/.X11-unix/X{display.lstrip(':')}"
+    while time.time() < deadline:
+        if os.path.exists(sock_path):
+            return True
+        time.sleep(0.1)
+    return False
+
+
+def grab_frame(display, out_path):
+    subprocess.run(
+        [
+            "ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error",
+            "-f", "x11grab", "-video_size", f"{SCREEN_W}x{SCREEN_H}",
+            "-i", display,
+            "-frames:v", "1", str(out_path),
+        ],
+        check=True,
+        timeout=20,
+    )
+
+
+def wait_for(path, client, timeout, what):
+    deadline = time.time() + timeout
+    while time.time() < deadline:
+        if path.exists():
+            return
+        if client.poll() is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"client exited early with code {client.returncode}")
+        time.sleep(0.1)
+    raise RuntimeError(f"timed out waiting for {what}")
+
+
+def run_scenario(workdir: Path, shots_dir: Path):
+    """Launches Xvfb + the real client, captures the screenshots of every view.
+    Returns {view: [(path, seconds since the first view-A frame), ...]}."""
+    worldpath = workdir / "world"
+    if worldpath.exists():
+        shutil.rmtree(worldpath)
+    (worldpath / "worldmods").mkdir(parents=True)
+    shutil.copytree(
+        HERE / "worldmods" / "sprite_probe",
+        worldpath / "worldmods" / "sprite_probe",
+    )
+    # The client's "--go"-with-a-fresh-world path resolves the game id purely
+    # from an on-disk world.mt (it does not honor --gameid for a world that
+    # doesn't exist yet), so write one ourselves instead of relying on the
+    # main menu's "create world" flow to do it.
+    (worldpath / "world.mt").write_text(
+        "\n".join([
+            "world_name = harvest_c01",
+            "gameid = devtest",
+            "backend = sqlite3",
+            "player_backend = sqlite3",
+            "auth_backend = sqlite3",
+            "mod_storage_backend = sqlite3",
+            "creative_mode = false",
+            "enable_damage = true",
+            "",
+        ])
+    )
+
+    client_conf = workdir / "client.conf"
+    client_conf.write_text(
+        "\n".join([
+            f"screen_w = {SCREEN_W}",
+            f"screen_h = {SCREEN_H}",
+            "fullscreen = false",
+            "fps_max = 30",
+            "fps_max_unfocused = 30",
+            "vsync = false",
+            "enable_minimap = false",
+            "show_debug = false",
+            "enable_sound = false",
+            "enable_fog = false",
+            "antialiasing = none",
+            "smooth_lighting = false",
+            "performance_tradeoffs = true",
+            "curl_verify_cert = false",
+            "",
+        ])
+    )
+
+    env = dict(os.environ)
+    env.update({
+        "DISPLAY": DISPLAY_NUM,
+        "LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE": "1",
+        "SDL_AUDIODRIVER": "dummy",
+        "ALSOFT_DRIVERS": "null",
+    })
+
+    xvfb = subprocess.Popen(
+        ["Xvfb", DISPLAY_NUM, "-screen", "0", f"{SCREEN_W}x{SCREEN_H}x24", "-nolisten", "tcp"],
+    )
+    try:
+        if not wait_for_x(DISPLAY_NUM):
+            raise RuntimeError("Xvfb did not start")
+
+        ready_file = worldpath / "probe_ready"
+        error_file = worldpath / "probe_error"
+        client = subprocess.Popen(
+            [
+                MINETEST_BIN,
+                "--config", str(client_conf),
+                "--go",
+                "--world", str(worldpath),
+                "--gameid", "devtest",
+                "--info",
+            ],
+            env=env,
+            cwd=str(workdir),
+        )
+        try:
+            deadline = time.time() + 90
+            while time.time() < deadline:
+                if error_file.exists():
+                    raise RuntimeError("world mod reported an error setting up the probe scene")
+                if ready_file.exists():
+                    break
+                if client.poll() is not None:
+                    raise RuntimeError(f"client exited early with code {client.returncode}")
+                time.sleep(0.2)
+            else:
+                raise RuntimeError("timed out waiting for probe_ready")
+
+            # view A: a time series
+            t_ready = time.time()
+            shots = {"A": [], "B": [], "C": []}
+            i = 0
+            while time.time() - t_ready < SAMPLE_WINDOW:
+                out = shots_dir / f"A_{i:03d}.png"
+                t_shot = time.time()
+                grab_frame(DISPLAY_NUM, out)
+                shots["A"].append((out, t_shot - t_ready))
+                i += 1
+                next_t = t_ready + i * SAMPLE_INTERVAL
+                delay = next_t - time.time()
+                if delay > 0:
+                    time.sleep(delay)
+
+            # views B and C: a few frames each once the player has turned
+            for view in ("B", "C"):
+                (worldpath / "view_request").write_text(view + "\n")
+                wait_for(worldpath / f"view_{view}_ready", client, 20, f"view {view}")
+                time.sleep(0.8)
+                for k in range(VIEW_SAMPLES):
+                    out = shots_dir / f"{view}_{k:03d}.png"
+                    grab_frame(DISPLAY_NUM, out)
+                    shots[view].append((out, time.time() - t_ready))
+                    time.sleep(0.25)
+            return shots
+        finally:
+            client.terminate()
+            try:
+                client.wait(timeout=10)
+            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+                client.kill()
+                client.wait(timeout=10)
+    finally:
+        xvfb.terminate()
+        try:
+            xvfb.wait(timeout=5)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            xvfb.kill()
+
+
+def animation_problems(series, ref=None):
+    """Problems with an animated probe's colour series [(t, name), ...] (tail of the window).
+
+    The probe must keep cycling through the sheet's frames in order
+    (yellow -> red -> magenta -> blue -> yellow ...), at about one frame per
+    FRAME_LENGTH, and -- if a reference series sampled from the same frames is
+    given -- show the same frame as the reference most of the time.
+    """
+    names = [n for _, n in series]
+    problems = []
+    if len(set(names)) < 2:
+        return [f"color stopped changing (animation is frozen): {names}"]
+    changes = 0
+    for (t0, a), (t1, b) in zip(series, series[1:]):
+        if a == b:
+            continue
+        changes += 1
+        # samples less than one frame apart can only see the next frame
+        if t1 - t0 < 0.9 * FRAME_LENGTH and b != CYCLE[(CYCLE.index(a) + 1) % len(CYCLE)]:
+            problems.append(f"frame {a} was followed by {b} (expected order {CYCLE})")
+    span = series[-1][0] - series[0][0]
+    expected = span / FRAME_LENGTH
+    if not (expected * 0.5 - 1 <= changes <= expected * 1.5 + 1):
+        problems.append(f"{changes} frame changes in {span:.1f} s, expected about {expected:.0f}")
+    if ref is not None:
+        ref_names = [n for _, n in ref]
+        same = sum(1 for a, b in zip(names, ref_names) if a == b) / len(names)
+        if same < 0.7:
+            problems.append(f"shows a different frame than an identical unattached camera-facing "
+                            f"sprite started at the same time in {100 - 100 * same:.0f}% of the samples")
+    if problems:
+        problems.append(f"sequence = {names}")
+    return problems
+
+
+def evaluate(shots):
+    results = {}
+    if len(shots["A"]) < 4:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"only captured {len(shots['A'])} frames, need at least 4")
+    # Drop the first couple of samples: right after "ready" the world's
+    # lighting is still catching up (freshly generated chunks render
+    # black for a few tenths of a second before their light values
+    # settle), which would otherwise read as a bogus "color".
+    frames = [(Image.open(p), t) for p, t in shots["A"]][2:]
+    imgs = [im for im, _ in frames]
+
+    up_colors = [classify(dominant_color(im, UPRIGHT_BOX)) for im in imgs]
+    ref_colors = [classify(dominant_color(im, REF_BOX)) for im in imgs]
+    up_names = [c for c, d in up_colors]
+    ref_names = [c for c, d in ref_colors]
+    # A "close enough" match (small squared RGB distance) to some palette
+    # color at least once confirms the sample box is actually framing the
+    # textured quad (and not empty sky/background).
+    # Allow for the scene's ambient light dimming the texture's true
+    # colors by a roughly constant factor (observed ~20%); sky/background
+    # colors are an order of magnitude further from every palette entry.
+    PALETTE_MATCH_DIST = 9000
+    up_on_palette = any(d < PALETTE_MATCH_DIST for _, d in up_colors)
+    ref_on_palette = any(d < PALETTE_MATCH_DIST for _, d in ref_colors)
+
+    results["sprite_probe.upright_sprite_renders_a_palette_color"] = (
+        up_on_palette,
+        f"upright_sprite sample box never matched a palette color closely, saw {up_names}",
+    )
+    results["sprite_probe.reference_sprite_renders_a_palette_color"] = (
+        ref_on_palette,
+        f"reference sprite sample box never matched a palette color closely, saw {ref_names}",
+    )
+
+    # Animations: judged on the second half of the window, well after the
+    # scene settled (a frozen animation can show one or two early transitions
+    # before it locks onto a single stale frame).
+    tail = len(frames) // 2
+    times = [t for _, t in frames][tail:]
+
+    def tail_series(box):
+        return list(zip(times, [classify_shaded(dominant_color(im, box), PALETTE)[0] for im in imgs[tail:]]))
+
+    ref_series = tail_series(REF_BOX)
+    for key, box, what, sync in (
+        ("reference_sprite_animates", REF_BOX, "reference camera-facing sprite", False),
+        ("upright_sprite_animates", UPRIGHT_BOX, "upright_sprite", True),
+        ("attached_sprite_animates", ATTACHED_BOX, "camera-facing sprite attached to another object", True),
+        ("attached_upright_sprite_animates", ATTACHED_UPRIGHT_BOX, "upright_sprite attached to another object", True),
+        ("upright_sprite_follows_set_sprite", STEPPED_BOX, "upright_sprite whose frame is set by set_sprite() every second", False),
+    ):
+        problems = animation_problems(tail_series(box), ref_series if sync else None)
+        results[f"sprite_probe.{key}"] = (not problems, f"{what}: " + "; ".join(problems))
+
+    # Orientation of the four-quadrant texture.
+    for key, box, what in (
+        ("sprite_texture_is_not_mirrored", SPRITE_QUADS_BOX, "camera-facing sprite"),
+        ("upright_sprite_back_is_not_mirrored", UPRIGHT_BACK_BOX, "upright_sprite seen from its back"),
+        ("upright_sprite_front_is_not_mirrored", UPRIGHT_FRONT_BOX, "upright_sprite seen from its front"),
+    ):
+        seen = {corner: majority([classify_shaded(dominant_color(im, cbox), QUADS)[0] for im in imgs])
+                for corner, cbox in corners(box).items()}
+        bad = {k: v for k, v in seen.items() if v != k}
+        results[f"sprite_probe.{key}"] = (
+            not bad,
+            f"{what}: each corner of the quad should show the same corner of its texture, "
+            f"saw (screen corner: texture corner) {seen}",
+        )
+
+    # select_x_by_camera: each probe shows the column for the side facing the camera.
+    seen = {}
+    for view, boxes, expected in (("B", VIEW_B_BOXES, EXPECTED_B), ("C", VIEW_C_BOXES, EXPECTED_C)):
+        vimgs = [Image.open(p) for p, _ in shots[view]]
+        if not vimgs:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"no frames captured for view {view}")
+        for yaw_i, (box, want) in enumerate(zip(boxes, expected)):
+            got = majority([classify_shaded(dominant_color(im, box), COLUMNS)[0] for im in vimgs])
+            seen[f"view {view} yaw {90 * yaw_i}"] = (got, want)
+    bad = {k: v for k, v in seen.items() if v[0] != v[1]}
+    results["sprite_probe.camera_facing_sprite_shows_the_side_facing_the_camera"] = (
+        not bad,
+        "select_x_by_camera picked the wrong view (got, expected): "
+        + ", ".join(f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in bad.items()),
+    )
+    return results
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--junit-out", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--shots-dir", default=None,
+                     help="optional directory to keep the captured screenshots in (for debugging)")
+    ap.add_argument("test_ids", nargs="*")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+
+    requested = set(args.test_ids) if args.test_ids else set(ALL_TEST_IDS)
+
+    workdir = Path(os.environ.get("HARVEST_WORKDIR", "/tmp/harvest_c01_run"))
+    workdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    shots_dir = Path(args.shots_dir) if args.shots_dir else workdir / "shots"
+
+    results = {}  # test_id -> (passed, message)
+    harness_error = None
+    for attempt in range(1, ATTEMPTS + 1):
+        if shots_dir.exists():
+            shutil.rmtree(shots_dir)
+        shots_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        try:
+            results = evaluate(run_scenario(workdir, shots_dir))
+            harness_error = None
+            break
+        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
+            harness_error = f"attempt {attempt}: {e}"
+            print(f"harness error ({harness_error}); " +
+                  ("retrying" if attempt < ATTEMPTS else "giving up"), flush=True)
+
+    testsuite = ET.Element("testsuite", name="sprite_probe", tests=str(len(requested)))
+    failures = 0
+    for test_id in sorted(requested):
+        classname, _, name = test_id.rpartition(".")
+        tc = ET.SubElement(testsuite, "testcase", classname=classname, name=name)
+        if harness_error is not None:
+            failures += 1
+            ET.SubElement(tc, "error", message=harness_error)
+            continue
+        passed, message = results.get(test_id, (False, "unknown test id"))
